Items.Authors: Ana Pérez Calpena, Ernesto Sanchez-Blanco, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Gerardo Veredas, Manuel Maldonado, Maria Penataro, Jesus Gallego, Africa Castillo, Armando Gil de Paz, Thomas Augusteijn, Gavin Dalton, Kacem El Hadi, Marie Larrieu, Alessandro Meoli, Roser Pello, Mathieu Puech, Myriam Rodrigues, Ruben Sanchez-Janssen, Hermine Schnetler, Jay Stephen, Christian Surace
Items.Title: MOSAIC for ELT: NIR spectrograph system performance
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object and multi-IFU spectrograph for the ESO-ELT in the range 0.39 to 1.8 microns that will provide survey observations. MOSAIC will collect the light from mIFU and MOS subapertures and drive it through the corresponding fiber links to the VIS and NIR spectrographs attached on the Nasmyth platform.   We present the optical and mechanical design and performance of the two NIR identical spectrographs, receiving each half of the fibers from the 180 NIR MOS targets, 630 fibers per spectrograph, and from the 8 mIFU, 672 fibers per spectrograph. Each spectrograph allows simultaneous coverage of J and H bands (0.95 to 1.80 microns) at low resolution (R~4000), and provides high resolution (R~18000) in the H band (1.52 – 1.62 microns). Each spectrograph hosts two cryo-mechanisms: The Entrance Focal Plane, to select between mIFU and MOS slits, an the LR/HR exchanger to select the grating in the H band.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Meoli, Domingo Álvarez Méndez, Thomas Augusteijn, Meghna Mohamed, Jay Stephan, Gavin Dalton, Kacem El Hadi, Myriam Rodrigues, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Marie Larrieu, Roser Pello, Mathieu Puech, Christian Surace, Rubén Sánchez Janssen, Hermine Schnetler
Items.Title: MOSAIC on ELT: detector trade-offs for the VIS and NIR channels
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC, the multi-object spectrograph for the ELT, is advancing through its preliminary design phase. Its distributed architecture, with over twenty-five interconnected subsystems, places stringent demands on the detector systems, which strongly influence optical throughput, focal-plane geometry, and thermal/electronic performance. We present a coordinated assessment of the visible (VIS) and near-infrared (NIR) detector options. For VIS, we examine large-format CCD technologies and the trade-off between quantum efficiency and focal-plane tiling constraints. For NIR, we compare H4RG configurations and their behaviour at 40 K and 80 K. The study outlines how each option shapes performance, risk, and integration complexity for the next MOSAIC design phases.

Items.Authors: Cyril Pannetier, Audrey A. Lanotte, Andreas Kelz, Carlos Enrique Rodriguez Alvarez, Yevgeniy Ivanisenko, Philippe Laporte, François Wildi, Daniel Schaerer, Isabelle Guinouard
Items.Title: MOSAIC on ELT: overview of the fibre system
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object fibre spectrograph for ESO's 39-m Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) which is providing spectroscopic multiplex capabilities at moderate spectral resolution (LR ; R∼4000-5000) and higher resolution (HR ; R∼18000), from the blue wavelengths (>0.39μm) to the near-infrared bandwidth (<1.8μm). MOSAIC offers four observational modes: visible and near-infrared multi-object spectroscopy (MOS), with configurations specific to LR and HR in visible range, and spatially resolved integral-field spectroscopy (mIFU).  This article presents an overview of the different fibre links with a description of their designs and associated components.

Items.Authors: Gavin B. Dalton, Myriam Rodrigues, Roser Pello, Kacem El Hadi, Mathieu Puech, Jurgen Schmoll, Tim Morris, Jeff Lynn, Thomas Augusteijn, Meghna Mohamed, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Ana Pérez Calpena, Walter Seifert, Wenli Xu, Nazim Bharmal, Ruben Sanchez-Janssen, Jay Stephan
Items.Title: MOSAIC, the ELT multi-object spectrograph: development and evolution of the instrument architecture and capabilities
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object spectrograph (MOS) for the 39-meter Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) of the European Southern Observatory (ESO). We present the evolution of the instrument concept from its initial conception through to the final design concept that will be presented at PDR. The evolution of the design by incorporation of per-target compensation for atmospheric dispersion has provided a route to conformance with tight restrictions on mass and volume, whilst at the same time expanding the overall efficiency of the instrument in terms of functionality and information gathering power.

Items.Authors: Jürgen Schmoll, Diane Chapuis-Kerouanton, Gavin Dalton, Malak Galal, Ian Lewis, Maxime Rombach, Ellen Schallig, Markus Thurneysen, Alec York, Louis Gabarra, Michaela Hirschmann, Jean-Paul Kneib
Items.Title: MOSAIC, the ELT multi-object spectrograph: Positioners with integrated atmospheric dispersion correction
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object fibre spectrograph for ESO's 39-m Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). It offers unique capabilities for a gigantic telescope in terms of multiplexing, wavelength coverage and spectral resolution. MOSAIC covers the visible (0.39-0.95 microns) and NIR (0.95-1.8 microns) wavelength domains. It has been designed to cover the largest possible area (~40 arcmin²) on the ELT focal plane.  This paper focuses on the optical realisation of the robotic arms designed to pick the light from the curved, non-telecentric focal surface while providing individual atmospheric dispersion correction for each of the 261 probes. Further challenges of the design are the large wavelength range and the tight tolerances necessary for an efficient optical fibre injection. An optical setup to test prototypes and to characterize the batch produced positioners will be introduced, allowing each individual pickoff arm to reach the tight tolerances for pointing accuracy and pupil stability.

Items.Authors: Lulu Qian, Min Huang, Guangming Wang, Yixin Zhao, Zhanchao Wang
Items.Title: Near Space Balloon-based Corona Observation Payload Design and Analysis
Items.Abstract: This paper introduces the design and analysis of the coronal observation payload cabin. To ensure the safe recovery of the observation payload when the payload module lands after the experiment, a finite element-based impact mechanics analysis was carried out. The simulation results show that the design of the payload module can effectively mitigate the landing impact and provide reliable protection for the payload. On this basis, we conducted a flight experiment, achieving a flight altitude of 30 km and a flight duration of approximately 3 hours. The experiment results indicate that the payload module functioned properly, effectively guaranteeing the data acquisition of the coronal observation payload. After the experiment, the coronagraph landed in good condition with normal functionality..

Items.Authors: Karen Tateoka, Hayato Takakura, Yutaro Sekimoto, Rion Takahashi, Frederick Matsuda, Shugo Oguri
Items.Title: Near-field polarisation angle measurement for wide field-of-view millimeter-wave telescopes
Items.Abstract: Accurate calibration of a telescope's polarisation angle is crucial for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) B-mode observations to mitigate the leakage from E-mode.    In this work, we investigate a polarisation angle calibration method based on a near-field measurement.  The amplitude and phase distributions scanned on a plane near the aperture were Fourier-transformed to obtain the antenna patterns, including the far sidelobes.  We present the polarisation angles of a crossed-Dragone telescope, determined from the measured co- and cross-polarisation patterns.    By employing holographic phase-retrieval techniques (R. Takahashi et al., 2024, Proc. SPIE, 13102), near-field measurements can be performed on a telescope with bolometric detectors such as LiteBIRD.  It offers the prospect of reconstructing the antenna patterns of thousands of detectors within a single scan.

Items.Authors: Roberta Pellegrini, Piero Gregori, Francesco Cerutti, Francesco Diprima, Ernesto Dölling, Emiliano Cordelli, Luca Conversi, Dora Föhring
Items.Title: NEO Flyeye network: from the commissioning of the OHB-I Flyeye-1 to the future Flyeye-2 deployment
Items.Abstract: The Flyeye telescope, developed by OHB Italia for ESA’s Space Safety Programme, achieved first light in May 2025, becoming the first operational compound-eye survey telescope for planetary defence. Its 1m mirror feeds 16 independent channels, achieving 1.5arcsec/px resolution and a 45deg² FoV, enabling high-cadence, wide-area coverage that traditional narrow-field telescopes cannot provide.   Commissioning activities at ASI Matera site validated system integration, detectors synchronization and data-flow, with successful detections of known NEO, even if not yet operating at nominal alignment. After acceptance, Flyeye will be installed on Mt. Mufara by late 2026 as key element of ESA’s NEO survey. The NEO survey strategy foresees to image each field four times per night with ~20-minute revisits, covering the visible sky to V≈21.5 every 2–3 nights and significantly improving warning times for 10-40m size impactors.  A second-generation Flyeye is planned for Chile to enhance global coverage

Items.Authors: Camilo Weinberger, Elena Masciadri, Alessio Turchi, Marlène de Sepibus, Angel Otarola, Steffen Mieske, Christian Veillet, Sam Ragland
Items.Title: Neural networks applied to forecasting the astroclimatic parameters in an operational context
Items.Abstract: The forecasting of optical turbulence is a crucial goal for astronomical ground-based observations for science operational optimization. Current research in this area identified autoregressive (AR) models as the best performers so far, achieving an RMSE of about 0.1″ for seeing forecasts on a time scale of 1h however neural networks (NN) remain extremely appealing as they are very flexible and they can be applied in contexts where the AR can not be used. It is therefore interesting to investigate characteristics of such an approach particularly in a forecasting operational context. We extend here our analysis to current NN algorithms beyond RF specifically developed for time series therefore for the forecast context. Our goals are to identify the best performances achievable with neural networks and the best operational configuration. This study is carried out within the framework of the FATE and ALTA projects, applied respectively to the VLT and LBT.

Items.Authors: Matthias Seidel, Alexander Rüde, Mathias Richerzhagen
Items.Title: NGCII detector controller synchronization using the White Rabbit protocol
Items.Abstract: Accurate synchronization between detector controllers is relevant for low-noise readout in focal-plane arrays. ESO’s new detector controller NGCII uses White Rabbit to enable sub-nanosecond timing accuracy and timestamp distribution in a PTP environment. In this presentation, we describe the method used to integrate White Rabbit into the NGCII architecture and show first lab results.

Items.Authors: Gabriele Umbriaco, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Maria Bergomi, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Tom Herbst, Remon van Gaalen, Roberto Ragazzoni, Valentina Viotto, Luca Cortese, Jacopo Farinato, Luca Marafatto, Silvio Di Rosa, Marco Dima, Davide Greggio, Florian Briegel, Lars Mohr, Thomas Bertram, Peter Bizenberger, Simone Antoniucci, Al Conrad, Alessio Caratti o Garatti, Gianluca Li Causi, Fernando Pedichini, Fabrizio Massi, Roberto Piazzesi, Sam Ragland
Items.Title: NirvanaVIS@LBT: AO-assisted speckle holography and bispectrum analysis
Items.Abstract: We present an analysis of speckle holography applied to short-exposure stellar images obtained with the Copernico 1.82 m telescope at Asiago Observatory. These data provide a reference dataset for developing and validating NirvanaVIS post-processing algorithms based on autocorrelation and bispectrum analysis. In NirvanaVIS, ground-layer adaptive optics will further improve data quality. Individual frames were pre-processed and analysed via Fourier-domain speckle reconstruction to evaluate the achievable diffraction-limited performance. We assess phase-retrieval and holographic reconstruction methods under development for NirvanaVIS, extending their applicability to smaller telescope diameters and higher-seeing conditions. Metrics such as FWHM, contrast, and binary-star separation accuracy quantify reconstruction fidelity. Results show that Copernico data represent suitable test cases for calibrating and optimising future AO-assisted speckle imaging pipelines for NirvanaVIS at LBT.

Items.Authors: Jonathan Dray, Kyliann Robert, Cyril Petit, Morgan Gray, Jalo Nousiainen, Baptiste Sinquin, Hisham Forrière, Armin Schimpf, Julien Charton, Thierry Fusco, Benoit Neichel
Items.Title: Numerical comparisons of VAR LQG-based predictive AO control and reinforcement-learning–based control methods for LEO-to-ground telecommunication links
Items.Abstract: In the field of adaptive optics for telecommunications with LEO satellites, new control methods emerge to counteract the specific turbulence effects encountered for these types of optical links. Here, we propose to compare numerically, with  end-to-end simulations, VAR LQG control and reinforcement-learning-based control in a variety of turbulence conditions.

Items.Authors: Romain J. L. Fétick, Arnaud Striffling, Matteo Pasinetti, Vincent Chambouleyron, Taissir Héritier
Items.Title: Observation of extended objects with a pyramid wavefront sensor: on-sky validation with the PAPYRUS AO system
Items.Abstract: The pyramid wavefront sensor (WFS) high sensitivity makes it the perfect candidate for future instruments such as the European ELT/HARMONI, or the French OHP/PROVIDENCE with satellite tracking ability. However, the object spatial extension dramatically reduces the pyramid sensitivity, even questioning its usage on extended objects.    We present here the loss of sensitivity due to object extension and show the possibility to compensate for the optical gains and retrieve the aberrant turbulence phase with fidelity for improved AO performances. We show the possibility to use the pyramid WFS on extended object through simulations, but also thanks to on-sky experiments with the PAPYRUS adaptive optics bench installed at Observatoire de Haute Provence.    The first results validate the use of a GSC for future instruments such as PCS to be installed at ELT. It also provides a baseline for operations of the pyramid WFS on extended objects with applications for HARMONI or PROVIDENCE.

Items.Authors: Luis Caniguante, Jorge Ramirez
Items.Title: Obsolescence-driven upgrade of the VLT M1 Cell Earthquake Detector using a COTS and functional safety strategy
Items.Abstract: The Earthquake Detector (EQD) protects the VLT’s primary mirror (M1) during strong seismic events or abnormal mechanical motion. The M1 mirrors are unique optical components produced specifically for the VLT, making reliable protection essential. After more than twenty years of service, the original EQD became highly obsolete due to aging custom electronics and unavailable spare parts. This work presents a complete upgrade of the EQD using modern Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) technologies and a fail-safe PLC platform. The new design improves reliability, simplifies maintenance, and ensures long-term operability. By maintaining the protection of a key optical component, the upgraded EQD contributes to the sustained performance and operational continuity of the VLT.

Items.Authors: Deborah Busonero, Alberto Riva, Mario Gai, Alessandro Sozzetti, Matteo Pinamonti, Mauro Focardi, Pierpaolo Merola, Vladimiro Noce, Jesper Skottfelt, David Hall, Daniele Gallieni, Alberto Vecchiato, Ummi Abbas, Marcello Agostino Scalera, Fabrizio Fornasiero, Chiara Scandaglia, Marina Vela Nuñez, Simone Chiarucci, Alessandro Grasso
Items.Title: OCEAN: a space telescope for Orbit Characterization of near-by Exoplanets by Astrometric determinatioN on a cubesat enviroment
Items.Abstract: The paper presents the current status and technological advancements of OCEAN (Orbit Characterization of near-by exoplanetary systems by Astrometric determinatioN) mission. The mission is conceived as a 36 U Cubesat, aiming at rapid implementation with a compact telescope designed for high stability and low sensitivity to perturbations, ensuring 1-μas systematic floor. The payload relies on a single-aperture, highly-stable space telescope enforcing circular symmetry on the whole optical system, down to the detector populating an annular region of uniform diffraction limited imaging. The payload is compact, light, and cheap. OCEAN represents a transformative step toward democratizing space-based based astrometry and exoplanet discovery. The mission combines scientific ambition with engineering pragmatism. It builds on existing CubeSat heritage while pushing the limits of precision and stability, potentially unlocking a new class of affordable, targeted astronomical observatories.

Items.Authors: Juan Larrain, Rodrigo Brito, Thomas Abbott
Items.Title: OCRO: an AI-class data center for the ALMA observatory
Items.Abstract: Systems engineering and project management approach to the design and construction of an AI class data center for the ALMA radio telescope in northern Chile. The new facility will house the next-generation correlator, supplying it with electrical power, cooling water, and conditioned air. Globally distributed stakeholders and an operating observatory at an elevation of 2950 m add to the complexity of the project.

Items.Authors: Aditi Gangadharan, Yasmine Meziani, Drew M. Miles, James H. Tutt, Jake A. McCoy, Ross C. McCurdy, Alexandra N. Higley, Randall L. McEntaffer
Items.Title: OGREs can see: synchrotron-based diffraction efficiency testing of OGRE diffraction gratings
Items.Abstract: The Off-plane Grating Rocket Experiment (OGRE) is a sounding rocket mission designed to obtain high-resolution soft X-ray spectra of Capella in the 0.2-2.0 keV band while demonstrating next-generation technologies for soft X-ray spectroscopy. A central enabling technology for the payload is modules of radially profiled, blazed off-plane reflection gratings. Achieving high diffraction efficiency, specifically a minimum design target of ~40% near 825 eV, is essential for meeting OGRE’s spectral throughput requirements. We present the methodology and results of absolute diffraction-efficiency measurements for multiple prototype variants of the OGRE master grating, performed at the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. These prototypes sample variations in grating geometry and blaze configuration as part of an iterative optimization process toward the mission’s efficiency goals. The measurements reported here provide key performance metrics that guide the ongoing

Items.Authors: Claudio Arena, Giuseppe Leto, Alessio Trois, Julien Cailleaux, Vito Conforti, Gianluca Giavitto, Luigi Lessio, Giovanni Lombardo, Cesare Molfese, Nicola La Palombara, Salvatore Scuderi, Gino Tosti
Items.Title: On-factory testing of the SST Telescopes for CTAO
Items.Abstract: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) will be composed of two arrays of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, with three different types of telescopes. The small-sized telescopes (SSTs, 37 units) are developed by an international consortium of institutes that will provide them as an in-kind contribution to CTAO. SSTs will be installed in Paranal (Chile) as part of the South site.    In this contribution we present the initial AIT/V activities carried out on the first SST units, with a focus on the on-factory test campaign. The activities span from safety aspects of the SSTs, testing of the various interfaces, functional and performance validation, and the evaluation of maintenance procedures foreseen during CTAO operations.  The AIT/V workflow is framed within the heritage of the ASTRI program, with a focus on how on-factory activities simplify and de-risk the subsequent on-site testing, verification and commissioning phases.

Items.Authors: Megan M. Dubay, Thomas Procter, William Marshall, Hank Corbett, Nicholas M. Law, Alex Bucheli, Jonathan Carney, James Dockery, Shannon Fitton, Lawrence Machia, Michael Ronco, Donovan G. Schlekat, Alan Vasquez Soto, Glenn Walters
Items.Title: On-sky verification of simulated performance of the Argus Array all-sky survey
Items.Abstract: The Argus Array is an all-sky survey instrument with the effective area of an 8m telescope. It will image 8,000sq-degrees of sky as often as once a second. Detailed optical simulations show that the 1200-telescope array will reach at least magnitude g=20.0 in a single 60s exposure with 1.0” pixel scale. We performed in-situ testing of the optical and imaging components as verification of the predicted performance for the integrated system, effects on performance for varying atmospheric conditions, and as a test of the internal acceptance testing process. Testing of the f/2.8 28cm OTAs and the custom 100-megapixel IMX461 cameras occurred during two consecutive new moon periods. Here we discuss the equipment, testing procedures, analysis methods, and findings.

Items.Authors: Francesco Di Mille, Povilas Palunas, David Osip, Guillermo Blanc, Marcelo Mora
Items.Title: Operational Status and Instrument Suite Development at the Magellan Telescopes
Items.Abstract: The Magellan telescopes at Las Campanas Observatory continue to evolve as the Carnegie Institution for Science partnership with Harvard/Smithsonian CfA, the University of Arizona, MIT, and the University of Michigan passes twenty years of operations. We present an updated view of the instrumentation suite and science operations at the 6.5-m Baade and Clay telescopes. Baade now hosts five permanently mounted, always-available instruments. At Clay, the second Nasmyth port is being converted from a fixed to a flexible interface to support longer, more continuous instrument availability. Over the past two years, three IFU instruments have been integrated, significantly expanding spatially resolved spectroscopy. We summarize recent performance trends, reliability considerations, and operational lessons from this configuration, and outline ongoing modernization efforts to meet the evolving needs of the Magellan user community.

Items.Authors: Martin Tschimmel, William Rambold, Gaetano Sivo, Masen Lamb, Vincent Garrel, Julia Scharwächter, Tim Gaggstatter, Jed Diller, Claudio Gaspar, Pablo Prado, Suresh Sivanandam
Items.Title: OpsCon vs. ConOps for GNAO-GIRMOS
Items.Abstract: Two adaptive optics systems working together: this presentation describes how GNAO and GIRMOS use Operations Concept (OpsCon) documents to bridge the high-level, science-driven Concept of Operations (ConOps) and the detailed operational steps needed by software developers and engineers. We outline the structure of the OpsCon hierarchy, show how complex activities such as adaptive optics loop closure are decomposed into implementable functions, and highlight how this approach revealed missing requirements and subsystems in the GNAO–GIRMOS design. The methodology is general and can be applied to other complex observatory and engineering systems.

Items.Authors: Anthony J. Shipp, Abigail Heins, Ethan Pascuales, Joshua A. Franklin, Keller Powell, Julian Pallini, Maria A. Chytka, Cailin Bain, Carter Stevens, Samuel G. Arnold, Gang Wang
Items.Title: Optical characterization and field testing of InfraTracker: next generation near infrared and visible light star tracker for suborbital sounding rocket flight
Items.Abstract: InfraTracker delivers a low-cost, first of its kind visible and infrared light star tracker assembly that increases performance while lowering resource usage for the cutting edge of defense and space research. The mission is focused on designing a compact, low-cost, and reusable star tracker using visible to near infrared light, from primarily COTS components. InfraTracker will utilize a Terrier-Improved Malemute sounding rocket out of NASA Wallops Flight Facility (WFF) as part of the RockSat program, allowing for observations to be made above most of Earth’s atmosphere allowing for flight qualification in space.

Items.Authors: Grace Piroscia, Connor Langford, Peter Tuthill, Christopher Betters, Frans Snik
Items.Title: Optical testbed and performance evaluation of large liquid-crystal diffractive optics
Items.Abstract: The TOLIMAN space telescope mission targets revolutionary performance in precision astrometric monitoring of binary stars to detect orbiting companions at micro-arcsecond levels of precision. A key enabling technology is a 125mm diameter patterned diffractive transmission plate with precisely aligned liquid crystal (LC) axes. Assembly of the flight-ready LC TOLIMAN poses immediate challenges to maintain optical transmitted wavefront quality. Along with this, LC polarisation degradation due to temperature and UV exposure is not well understood in an Earth orbit context. Using an optical testbed at the University of Sydney, this paper presents methodologies and outcomes in the pathway to furnish a flight-qualified LC diffractive pupil.

Items.Authors: Alireza Vafa, Alireza Basohbat Novinzadeh
Items.Title: Optical/IR interferometry in space: evolution of concepts and missions
Items.Abstract: Distributed optical and infrared interferometry in space combines light from multiple telescopes to reach the angular resolution of a much larger virtual aperture, opening regimes inaccessible to current monolithic or segmented observatories. This paper reviews the evolution of space-based optical/IR interferometry, from early concepts such as Bracewell’s nulling interferometer and Labeyrie’s hypertelescope to major mission studies including Darwin, TPF, SIM, SI, and ST3/StarLight. We examine their science goals, architectures, and the technological and programmatic challenges that limited their implementation. We then highlight 2010s advances in formation flying, precision metrology, nulling and beam-combining testbeds, and hypertelescope prototypes, as well as synergies with ground-based facilities. Finally, we discuss recent mission concepts such as LIFE, SPIRIT, and SPECS, and outline a staged, technology-driven roadmap toward future pathfinder and flagship space interferometers.

Items.Authors: Danny Gasman, Janus D. Brink, Kieran Leschinski, Gilles Otten, Hugo Buddelmeijer, Roy van Boekel, Oliver Czoske, Wolfgang Kausch
Items.Title: Optimal spectral extraction for the METIS-LSS
Items.Abstract: The Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) is one of the first-light instruments of the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). As larger and more sensitive observatories are being built, the data reduction pipeline must improve to make sure the highest sensitivity is reached in the data. Aside from accurate instrument characterization, optimal extraction algorithms can be employed to improve the S/N in spectra. These algorithms rely on accurate characterization of the noise and point-spread function (PSF) on the detectors, to weigh the contributions of individual pixels in the extraction process, and naturally handle bad pixels. Optimal extraction is already set to be the standard approach for the ESO-METIS pipeline. However, the thermal background in the mid-infrared poses an additional challenge, as will the modelling of telluric lines. We must assess what will be required for the optimal extraction to work.

Items.Authors: Bradley S. Frank, Srikrishna Sekhar
Items.Title: Optimising continuum subtraction for SKA‑scale spectral imaging
Items.Abstract: Continuum subtraction is essential for spectral-line radio imaging, performed either in the visibilities or in the images. Visibility-based methods include fitting and subtracting the per-baseline continuum, or removing a continuum sky model built during self-calibration or imaging. Image-domain methods include pixel-wise polynomial fitting or median filtering. Although effective in many cases, modern wide-area, high-sensitivity surveys for the SKA and its pathfinders demand approaches that remain performant and robust under imperfect calibration, and that deliver high-fidelity spectral-line products. We present a much-needed reformulation of the continuum-subtraction problem from first principles, including a novel refactoring of visibility data and a prototype implementation demonstrating gains in processing time and dynamic range. We also show how advanced statistical techniques, such as Bayesian optimisation, can accelerate the procedure while preserving spectral-line fidelity.

Items.Authors: John Rankin, Stefano Basso, Sergio Campana, Marta Civitani, Paolo Conconi, Vincenzo Cotroneo, Giovanni Pareschi, Daniele Spiga
Items.Title: Optimization of X-ray optics for accurate gravitational wave transient localization
Items.Abstract: Current X-ray telescopes have a combination of field of view and angular resolution unsuitable to accurately localize the electromagnetic counterparts of gravitational wave events. This will become increasingly important when the LIGO and Virgo experiments will work at full sensitivity, when the Einstein Telescope observatory will come online, or with the space mission LISA, all in the next decade. With the goal of having a source localization accuracy of tens of arcsec over a ~10 square degrees field of view, together with hundreds of cm^2 effective area, we study how Lobster eye and Kirkpatrick-Baez optics can be optimized for this objective if appropriately-built, and also how Wolter-I optics can be appropriately modified. We compare the advantages and drawbacks of each optical design, in particular regarding the contribution of stray light.

Items.Authors: Ludwig von Dossow, Emilio Barrios, Héctor Alarcón, Patricio Álvarez, Eduardo Chaparro, Emiliano Galuppo, Christian García, Daniela Soto
Items.Title: Optimizing the Control Room environment: A review of teamwork and implementation stages at the ALMA Observatory
Items.Abstract: The construction and commissioning of observatory control rooms involve critical design stages. The ALMA Observatory has undertaken this process twice: for its remote control room in Santiago and, recently, for a new Operations Support Facility (OSF) room housing the ATAC correlator.    Beyond technical specifications, post-commissioning improvements focused on human factors were achieved through essential teamwork. The Array Operations Group consolidated feedback from diverse users, including Engineering and Outreach departments, to optimize the workspace. This paper reviews the resulting operational enhancements and demonstrates how this collaborative approach created a superior operating environment, providing valuable considerations for other scientific facilities.

Items.Authors: Yue Yu, Jooyun Woo, Marcela Stern, Julia K. Vogel, Jaime Ruz Armendariz, Marta M. Civitani, Stefano Basso, Peter L. Henriksen, Desiree D. M. Ferreira, Sonny Massahi, Kerstin Perez
Items.Title: Overview and design optimization of a custom hybrid X-ray telescope for the International Axion Observatory (IAXO)
Items.Abstract: Axions and axion-like particles (ALPs) are among the most compelling candidates for dark matter. The International Axion Observatory (IAXO) is a next-generation axion helioscope designed to search for axions and ALPs from the Sun that are reconverted into X-ray photons via strong magnetic fields, while BabyIAXO, a preliminary pathfinder experiment, will validate all key technologies at scale. Among the technologies, the focusing X-ray telescopes are essential to both take advantage of dramatically increased magnetic field volumes and to improve the signal-to-noise ratio at the detector. In this talk, We present an overview and design optimization of a custom hybrid optics for BabyIAXO, evaluate its performance, and summarize preliminary fabrication results.The optic is cost-effective and scalable, and is expected to achieve an effective area above 2000 cm² at 3 keV and to exceed 2500 cm² at 1 keV, with an ideal spatial resolution better than 1 arcminute.

Items.Authors: Jialin Li, Jordan M. Stone, Kevin R. Wagner, Steve Ertel, Feng Long, Laird M. Close
Items.Title: Packaging and demonstrating the LBTI/ALES pipeline: an efficient, user-friendly data reduction suite for high-contrast thermal-IR integral field spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: The Arizona Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy (ALES) is a thermal-infrared integral-field spectrograph operating within the 1–5 μm imaging camera LBTI/LMIRCam. We present a publicly available Python data-reduction pipeline for the ALES instrument, which is optimized for low-resolution (R~ 40) spectroscopy of directly imaged exoplanets and protoplanets in the 3-4 μm range. The pipeline implements the full reduction sequence, i.e., detector calibrations, lenslet spectral extraction, spectral-cube reconstruction, image selection and registration, and modular post processing for starlight subtraction. Portions of the core reduction framework build on earlier work (e.g. Stone et al. 2022, Wagner et al. 2023), which we have expanded and documented to support a broader user community and a wider range of science cases. We outline the reduction process and demonstrate its performance using on-sky observations of protoplanetary disks.

Items.Authors: Ioannis Argyriou, Roy van Boekel, Alistair C. H. Glasse, Eckhart Spalding, Danny Gasman, Riley Borthwick, Violeta Gámez Rosas, Daniel Dicken, Olivier Absil, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Oliver Czoske, Gilles Otten, Hugo Buddelmeijer, Janus D. Brink, Wolfgang Brandner, Jennifer L. Karr, Benjamin Eisele, Kieran Leschinski, Wim De Meester, Kwinten Missiaen, Bernhard R. Brandl
Items.Title: Paving the road to the top: preparations for the ELT-METIS system performance test campaign
Items.Abstract: The Mid-Infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) - first light instrument for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) - is in the process of assembly and integration in Leiden, The Netherlands. Following integration and alignment, the METIS (high-contrast) imaging and spectroscopic mode performance will be tested using the Warm Calibration Unit and Telescope Simulator. The vast number of METIS instrument configurations makes testing the performance of all the modes a unique challenge. Thankfully the instrument simulator ScopeSim allows to produce radiometrically-representative METIS detector images of the calibration sources for each mode. These data are used to develop the analysis tools, define test sequences, and determine initial exposure parameters. In this work we present the logical flow of the performance tests that will be carried out in Leiden as well as simulated data and performance analysis tools that will create the foundation for the activities in Europe and in Chile.

Items.Authors: Thomas Lechner, Todd Veach, Cynthia Froning, Andrew Peterson, Adam Thornton, Trent Peterson, Dana Koeppe
Items.Title: performance and detector characterization of SCORPIO for the Gemini South Observatory
Items.Abstract: SCORPIO is a multi-channel optical-infrared instrument for the Gemini South 8-meter telescope, providing spectroscopy (0.385-2.35 µm) and imaging (0.400-2.35 µm) across eight synchronized focal plane arrays. The system uses four Teledyne H2RG HgCdTe detectors and four Teledyne e2v CCDs, read out via archon and SIDECAR/MACIE electronics. A custom synchronization backplane distributes a master clock and triggers to all detectors, enabling 10 ms timing precision and 50 ms temporal resolution for rapid transient science. We present ongoing detector performance characterization, including H2RG response, readout stability, and cross-channel synchronization, as SCORPIO progresses towards integration and deployment at Gemini South.

Items.Authors: Viktoria Kutnohorsky, Robert J. Harris, Aurélien Benoît, David G. MacLachlan, Timothy A. Birks, Chiara D'Amato, Sajjad Mahdizadeh, Sebastiaan Haffert, Andrea Bianco, Joss Guy, Robert R. Thomson, Jared R. Males, Laird M. Close, Olivier Guyon
Items.Title: Performance estimates and target selection for the MCIFU, the Multi-Core Integrated Field Unit
Items.Abstract: The Multi-Core Integrated Field Unit (MCIFU) is a demonstrator for the ELT’s Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (PCS) and will achieve first light in 2026 on MagAO-X at the Magellan Clay telescope. To evaluate its performance, we developed a quantitative model incorporating atmospheric transmission, telescope and instrument throughput, and detector characteristics such as quantum efficiency, dark current, and readout noise. Based on this model, an exposure time calculator (ETC) was constructed to predict the signal-to-noise ratio under varying stellar magnitudes, integration times, and observing conditions. The ETC includes three source-spectrum options: continuum, blackbody, and reference spectra. It produces detailed SNR budgets across the Y, J, and H bands to identify observable targets. First-light photometric measurements in 2026 will aide to validate the model and help define the operational parameter space for future PCS observations on the ELT.

Items.Authors: Paul Hickson, Kuntal Misra, Jean Surdej, Bhavya Ailawadhi, Monalisa Dubey, Naveen Dukiya, Sara Filali, Priyanshi Kumari, Gokul S. Mehra, Vibhore Negi, Anna Pospieszalska-Surdej, Kumar Pranshu, Sarvesh K. Yadav
Items.Title: Performance of the International Liquid Mirror Telescope
Items.Abstract: The International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT) is a 4-meter zenith-pointing astronomical survey telescope. Located at Devasthal Peak in the Indian Himalayas, the project is a collaboration between institutions in Belgium, India and Canada. Its primary scientific program is the detection and study of transient and variable sources. A unique feature of the ILMT is its primary mirror which employs liquid mercury as the reflecting surface. Equipped with a 4096 x 4096 pixel CCD camera, the telescope records images of a 22 arcmin wide strip of sky passing overhead, revisiting every object in the strip each night for several months. The ILMT began operation in 2022, and has now obtained over 1900 hours of imaging data. We provide an overview of the project and discuss the performance of the telescope, including image quality, limiting magnitudes, observing statistics, data products and the transient detection success rate.

Items.Authors: Dawoon E. Kim, Alessandro Di Marco, Saba Imtiaz, Hemanth Manikantan, Ajay Ratheesh, Paolo Soffitta, Enrico Costa, Ettore Del Monte, Sergio Fabiani, Fabio La Monaca, Fabio Muleri, Alda Rubini
Items.Title: Performance of the Monte Carlo Simulation Tool for the Gas Pixel Detector in Three Dimensions
Items.Abstract: The Gas Pixel Detector in Three Dimensions (GPD3D) is a novel concept for the next generation of photoelectric-based X-ray polarimeters. This detector records the 3D photoelectron tracks in a gas chamber. It is expected to enhance the sensitivity and mitigate the limitations of the current Gas Pixel Detector. This advancement is enabled by a hybrid pixel detector readout chip, Timepix3, which measures both the timing and charge information of incident particles at the pixel level. Monte Carlo simulation is one of the most cost-effective and efficient approaches for investigating the performance of a new detector system under a wide range of conditions. In this context, we present a dedicated Monte Carlo simulation software package for GPD3D, constructed with the Geant4 toolkit, and evaluate its performance across different configurations with potential use in the next generation of X-ray polarimeters for astrophysics.

Items.Authors: Marie Tourneur-Silvain, Aurélia Secroun, Naomie De Araujo, Eric Kajfasz, Jean-Luc Atteia, Hervé Valentin, Francis Fortin
Items.Title: Performance Validation and Persistence Study of the ALFA SWIR Detector for SVOM’s GRB Science
Items.Abstract: The SVOM mission uses the Colibri telescope and its CAGIRE near-infrared camera to validate the first on-sky performance of the ALFA 2k×2k SWIR HgCdTe detector developed by Lynred and CEA-LETI. A dedicated optimization and characterization campaign on CPPM’s Pica platform demonstrated response uniformity, reduced CDS noise, and a well-calibrated linear dynamic range, confirming compliance with mission requirements. Persistence effects were measured in J and H bands, revealing wavelength-dependent persistence amplitudes, with a notable reduction when operating at a lower temperature. The study also introduces a new mission-specific persistence protocol, and confirms ALFA’s readiness for broader use in future infrared instruments.

Items.Authors: Joice Mathew
Items.Title: Performance Verification of Cryogenic Preamplifiers for Enhanced Sensitivity in Infrared Detector Systems
Items.Abstract: This study presents ongoing research at ANU on cryogenic preamplifier systems for infrared detectors, designed to improve signal integrity in systems with long cable runs. By amplifying and converting detector outputs to differential signals near the detector, the preamplifier mitigates RF interference and enhances readout performance. Acting as a buffer for ROIC outputs, it enables low-noise amplification close to the detector, improving sensitivity, frame rates, and SNR for astronomical observations. Laboratory tests assessed gain and readout noise using photon transfer curves and evaluated RF noise suppression under high-frequency interference, achieving over threefold reduction in external noise. As part of ANU’s detector and control ecosystem—including the compact Rosella readout system for space—the cryogenic preamplifier supports instruments like GMTIFS and future space-based infrared payloads.

Items.Authors: Romain Laugier, Lucas Labadie, Denis Defrère, Guillermo Martin, Marc-Antoine Martinod
Items.Title: Phase-sensing with the modified Mach-Zehnder nuller
Items.Abstract: Integrated-optics tricouplers are one of the rare nulling beam-combiners that can provide phase sensing in operation, but they lack a bulk optics equivalent.  With this work, we demonstrate how this sensing ability arises in the beam combination, and how it fundamentally comes at the cost of off-axis light. We then propose a novel alteration to the modified Mach-Zehnder topology (Serabyn 2001) of balanced beamsplitter to bring sensing capabilities by recycling light already shed by the combiner to balance intensity at no additional throughput cost. This new option offers a pivotal new architecture options for fine piston control accuracy and null maintenance with reduced overheads.

Items.Authors: Christophe Moins, Dan Popovic, Jose Antonio Abad, Constanza Araujo, Helen Bedigan, Martin Brinkmann, Elsa Calmette, Greidy Castellanos, Angela Cortes, Byron Engler, Christoph Frank, Fernando Gago, Elizabeth George, Thomas Grudzien, Ivan Guidolin, Andreas Haimerl, Peter Hammersley, Marcus Haug, Stefan Huber, Paul Jolley, Aglaé Kellerer, Mario Kiekebusch, Jean-Paul Kirchbauer, Barbara Klein, David Kosten, Johannes Kolmeder, Johan Kosmalski, Paolo La Penna, Ulrich Lampater, Serban Leveratto, Steffan Lewis, Christopher Mandla, Enrico Marchetti, Leander Mehrgan, Jérôme Paufique, Lorenzo Pettazzi, Oliver Pfuhl, Thomas Pfrommer, Malte Scherbarth, Sébastien Tordo, Pablo Zuluaga-Ramírez, Sara Zuccon
Items.Title: Phasing and Diagnostic Station (PDS) control software overview
Items.Abstract: The Phasing and Diagnostic Station (PDS) will host five visible and infrared cameras and their optomechanical components. It will be operated by control software based on the ICS framework (IFW).       The software comprises the following components: Observation Coordination System (OCS), Function Control System (FCS) to control and monitor hardware functions and sensing systems, Detector Control System (DCS) to manage the various wavefront sensor camera systems, Cryostat to maintain the infrared detector at low temperature, using the Cryogenic Control Systems software toolkit.       Control and engineering GUIs, along with templates executed through the IFW sequencer, will send commands to the system via standard interfaces.

Items.Authors: Hirofumi Okita, Naoyuki Tamura, Takashi Hattori, Yuhei Takagi, Yusei Koyama, Masayuki Kuzuhara
Items.Title: PI-type Instrumentation at the Subaru Telescope
Items.Abstract: We explain the PI-type Instrumentation activities at the Subaru Telescope. The Subaru Telescope has a framework for PI-type instruments, which are developed, assembled, integrated, tested, and operated using external funding and human resources to achieve specific science goals or demonstrate novel technology, and which complement with facility instruments that are developed, maintained, and operated by resources of the Subaru Telescope. In this paper, we summarize the carry-in procedure of the PI-type instruments, interface control with the telescope, and current status of PI-type instruments in the Subaru Telescope. We will also summarize the results of the productivity study and user opinions survey discussed at the PI-type instrument workshop held in October 2025.

Items.Authors: Katherine Laliotis, Pierre-François Léget, Aaron Roodman, Mike Jarvis, Theo Schutt, Joshua E. Meyers, Andrew P. Rasmussen
Items.Title: Point-spread function performance and systematic error sources in early LSSTCam observations
Items.Abstract: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s LSST will conduct a decade-long survey of the southern sky, enabling precision weak-lensing cosmology with the largest galaxy sample ever obtained. Because the weak-lensing signal is extremely small, the survey’s cosmological goals require tight control of systematic errors, particularly those arising from point-spread function (PSF) modeling. We present an assessment of the LSST Camera’s initial PSF performance during commissioning and early operations. We show the fidelity of initial PSF models, identify the dominant sources of PSF size residuals, and discuss implemented strategies to mitigate these effects. We conclude with an outlook on improving PSF modeling as LSST enters full survey operations.

Items.Authors: Jaya Chand
Items.Title: Polaris and Zenith non-tracking Differential Image Motion Monitors for robust atmospheric turbulence monitoring
Items.Abstract: Traditional DIMM seeing monitors depend on bright stars and accurate tracking mounts, increasing system cost, complexity, and maintenance.To address this, we present two wide-field, static, untracked DIMMs: the Polaris DIMM and the Zenith DIMM.These instruments aim to provide reliable Fried parameter measurements with minimal infrastructure and autonomous operation.The Polaris DIMM continuously observes Polaris without tracking but cannot operate in equatorial regions or the southern hemisphere.To achieve global applicability, the Zenith DIMM uses an even larger field of view with fixed pointing to function at any latitude.Both prototypes were installed on the ING DIMM tower at ORM, La Palma, where they showed good agreement with the ING robotic DIMM (R2D2).Using scintillation index and covariance, we also estimate a simple three-layer turbulence profile, from which the isoplanatic angle, and with wind information, the coherence time and photometric scintillation noise, can be derived.

Items.Authors: Antonin Besse, Imran Khan, Alexandra Mazzoli, Colin Dandumont, Ida Sigusch, Pierre Piron, Jérôme Loicq
Items.Title: Polarization aberrations in nulling interferometry: Exoplanet explorer case study
Items.Abstract: One of the objectives of modern astronomy is the characterization of terrestrial exoplanets orbiting Sun-like stars in the mid-infrared, where instruments face requirements that can only be overcome by nulling interferometry. However, optical effects such as polarization aberrations require careful attention for they deteriorate the null depth. Using the optical design of the Exoplanet Explorer concept study, we analyze the influence of polarization aberrations over the 3–20 μm band for multiple optical coatings, and, in addition, we describe multiple polarization aberrations compensation strategies and show their impact on the null depth. We present our nulling interferometry testbench, where we experimentally investigate polarization aberrations in the beam combiner and phase shifter to provide more insights into the required polarization considerations. These results will be used to implement polarization control subsystems in our 4 beams broadband nulling interferometry testbench.

Items.Authors: Federico Astori
Items.Title: POLOCALC and HoverCal drone system: attitude reconstruction software
Items.Abstract: Precise calibration of the absolute polarization angle is critical for detecting primordial B-mode signals in the cosmic microwave background. The POLOCALC and HoverCal projects operate drone-borne polarized microwave emitters (90–280 GHz) to provide a stable far-field reference for telescopes. The key innovation is the use of photogrammetry, tightly integrated with onboard sensors, to determine the drone’s attitude with extreme precision, directly linking the orientation of the emitted polarization signal to fixed ground references. Leveraging this technique, the system aims to achieve absolute polarization angle calibration with an accuracy of σΨ ~ 0.01°, sufficient for searching primordial B-modes at the level σ_r ~ 10⁻³. Photogrammetry is central to determining the polarization plane’s orientation in celestial coordinates, employing a sophisticated color-filtering algorithm and a Bayesian framework to retrieve the drone’s attitude within these stringent accuracy requirements.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo Cotroneo, Giovanni Pareschi, Stefano Basso, Marta M. Civitani, Thorsten Dohring, Eugenio Gibertini, Giorgia Sironi, Daniele Spiga
Items.Title: Polydopamine overcoatings for soft X-ray reflectivity enhancements: recent progress and performance assessment
Items.Abstract: We present recent advances in dopamine-based overcoatings to enhance the soft X-ray performance of grazing-incidence telescope mirrors. Thin polydopamine (PDA) films, deposited by dip-coating from aqueous solution, provide a carbon-rich, low-density layer on conventional high-Z coatings (e.g. Au, Ir, Ir/Cr), offering an attractive, lower-cost alternative to sputtered carbon or other carbon-based films (e.g. SiC, B₄C). We report an expanded set of laboratory and synchrotron reflectivity measurements, together with process optimization (thickness control, uniformity, reproducibility), tests on relevant mirror geometries, and an assessment of surface roughness and small-angle scattering. Ongoing environmental and adhesion studies, combined with updated optical modelling, support the potential application of these coatings in future cost-constrained spaceborne X-ray telescopes requiring large effective area in the soft band.

Items.Authors: Carlos M. Correia, Kyliann Robert, Cyril Petit, Jean-Marc Conan
Items.Title: Predictive atmospheric models for servo-lag mitigation in frozen-flow-dominated regimes: application to free space communications and high-contrast imagers
Items.Abstract: Adaptive Optics systems in Free-Space Optics (FSO) links and High Contrast Imaging are strongly limited by the system's servo-lag error. This work evaluates auto-regressive (AR) models that exploit the measurable temporal correlation in wavefront distortions to predict future turbulence states and enable to compensate for the system latency. A fully analytic framework is developed to estimate the residual error variance and determine the optimal AR order and prediction horizon under varying turbulence conditions and sampling rates. Experiments on ONERA’s PICOLO and LISA benches are presented where we tested the theoretical expectations. Results show in these high wind speed regimes large Strehl Ratio gains and improved FSO link stability.

Items.Authors: Asghar Jafarzadeh, Alexander Steiner, Ronny Sternberger, Markus Garczarczyk, Markus Schulze
Items.Title: Pre-shipment verification, components performance characterisation, system identification of the CTAO medium-sized telescope structure and its impact on on-site commissioning
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the pre-shipment verification approach developed for the Medium-Sized Telescope (MST) of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). Key MST structural components are pre-assembled in Berlin and tested before shipment overseas, at a stage where the components are not yet fully integrated and do not experience full operational loads. These controlled conditions enable early detection of mechanical, control-system, and integration issues. The study reports results from the first two MST pathfinder units, using synchronised sensor data, motor torque, encoder, and axis-position data collected through custom test software. The objectives include system identification, verification of control schemes and components, baseline measurements, and validation of monitoring and protection concepts. The findings support the definition of preliminary acceptance criteria for serial production and provide input for refining commissioning procedures for on-site assembly.

Items.Authors: Jorge Parra, Mario Castro
Items.Title: Prioritizing maintenance workforce effort in ground-based telescopes through Risk-Based Maintenance (RBM) Strategy.
Items.Abstract: Optimizing astronomical observatory uptime requires a prioritized, proactive maintenance approach. This paper proposes a Risk-Based Maintenance (RBM) framework to strategically allocate maintenance workforce and operational windows for ground-based telescopes. The methodology systematically identifies critical systems, assesses failure possibility and operational consequences, and incorporates current equipment status to calculate a comprehensive risk score. This score objectively ranks maintenance tasks, directing limited resources to the most critical components. This data-driven prioritization replaces traditional time-based or reactive methods, boosting telescope reliability and longevity. The discussion will cover RBM model development, integration with a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS), and expected benefits, including reduced downtime, optimized labor use, and maintenance standardization.

Items.Authors: Florian Kerber, Raul Cordero, Omar Cuevas, Susana Deustua, Patricio Galeas, Markus Gaug, Rory Gillespie, Miska Le Louarn, Julio C. Marin, Ricardo C. Munoz, Angel Otarola, Anna Francesca Pala, Jérôme Paufique, Joseph P. Rice, Roberto Rondanelli, Alain Smette, Roberta Zanin
Items.Title: Profiling of the Atmosphere by Remote Sensing and Radiosonde Balloon Launches above our Astronomical Observatory Sites - PARABOLAS
Items.Abstract: The European Southern Observatory (ESO) is teaming up with international partners to conduct a measurement campaign with the main objective of characterizing a significant volume of atmosphere above the Paranal (VLT), Armazones (ELT) and the future Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) South sites covering a horizontal distance of about 25 km between the observatory sites and an altitude of at least 15 km to address both its spatial and temporal variations using an array of in-situ and remote sensing instrumentation. The campaign’s results will be key for the science operations of ESO’s fully adaptive Extremely Large Telescope, and highly relevant for the NIST Stars project on Paranal, and for the CTAO which uses the atmosphere as its detection medium for gamma rays. The campaign is currently scheduled for 2026/27. We’ll report on the current status of planning and the next steps towards the actual implementation.

Items.Authors: Xiaoyun Ma, Ruirui Fan, Wei Wang, Nannan Yue, Xiangxiang Ren, Xaojing Wu, Yu Wang, Yuxin Qiu, Fei Liu, Hanzhang Wang, Ran Duan
Items.Title: Progress on a scalable FPGA-GPU heterogeneous 10k-Pixel TES/MKID readout
Items.Abstract: Although current frequency-division multiplexing umux TES/MKID readouts can achieve multiplexing ratios of thousands of pixels on a single signal line, large arrays of 10k or even 100k pixels still require multiple readout units. This work presents a 10k-pixels readout system implemented on an FPGA-GPU heterogeneous architecture. The FPGA handles the shared signal processing algorithms for both TES and MKID, while the GPU manages the remaining demodulation steps specific to each detector. This approach supports both detector types and facilitates development and debugging. This paper will also discuss the design and challenges of multi-unit systems within the heterogeneous architecture.
